title: Corporate Lawyer Salary: Hourly to Annual, Casual Loading and Super Explained
description: Convert a corporate lawyer salary from hourly to annual using Fair Work rates, casual loading, and super. Understand award minimums and typical earnings.
salarySummary: For a corporate lawyer earning the ABS full-time adult ordinary time rate of $54.83 per hour (38-hour week), the annual salary is approximately $108,352 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum corporate lawyer salary under the Legal Services Award?
faqs.a: The Legal Services Award 2020 does not have a classification specifically for 'corporate lawyer'. The highest clerical classification is Level 6 Law clerk at $36.03 per hour from 1 July 2026. Corporate lawyers are typically employed above award, so their salary is negotiated individually. The ABS full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026) provide a more realistic benchmark for a corporate lawyer salary.

faqs.q: How does casual loading apply to a corporate lawyer salary?
faqs.a: If a corporate lawyer is engaged as a casual employee under the Legal Services Award, they are entitled to a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. For example, a Level 6 law clerk casual rate would be $36.03 × 1.25 = $45.04 per hour. However, most corporate lawyers are full-time permanent employees and do not receive casual loading. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this loading works for award-covered roles.

faqs.q: Is superannuation paid on top of a corporate lawyer salary?
faqs.a: Yes, superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a corporate lawyer earning $108,352 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $13,002.24 in super. This is not deducted from the salary but added on top. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Corporate Lawyer Salary Conversion

When you hear about a **corporate lawyer salary**, it is often quoted as an annual figure. But if you are paid by the hour or considering a contract role, converting that hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time work, we assume 38 ordinary hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman for most awards, including the Legal Services Award 2020.

For example, if a corporate lawyer earns $54.83 per hour (the ABS full-time adult ordinary time earnings as of May 2026), the annual salary before tax and super is:

$54.83 × 38 × 52 = $108,352.08

This calculation gives you a gross annual figure. Remember, this assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting or comparing job offers.

### Award Rates vs. Market Rates for Corporate Lawyers

The Legal Services Award 2020 [MA000116] sets minimum pay rates for legal clerical and administrative employees. From 1 July 2026, the highest classification under the award is Level 6 Law clerk at $36.03 per hour. However, a **corporate lawyer salary** is typically well above award minimums. Corporate lawyers are often employed under enterprise agreements or individual contracts that reflect their specialised skills and experience.

For a realistic benchmark, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees in ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This translates to $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. Many corporate lawyers earn more than this average, especially in top-tier firms or with several years of experience.

### Casual Loading and Its Effect on Pay

If you are working as a casual corporate lawyer (less common but possible in some contract roles), you are entitled to a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate under the award. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains that this loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For a Level 6 law clerk, the casual rate would be $36.03 × 1.25 = $45.04 per hour. However, most corporate lawyers are permanent employees and do not receive casual loading. When using our [timesheet](/) or [pay guides](/blog), always enter your base hourly rate without casual loading; the tool will add it if you select the casual checkbox.

### Fortnightly Pay and Annual Salary

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For the corporate lawyer earning $54.83 per hour, weekly pay is $54.83 × 38 = $2,083.54, so fortnightly pay is $4,167.08. This is useful for budgeting and comparing to salary offers that are quoted fortnightly.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Corporate Lawyer Salary

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy of 2% applies to most taxpayers. For a gross salary of $108,352, the estimated tax is approximately $24,467 plus Medicare of $2,167, leaving a take-home pay of about $81,718. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed calculator.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional contribution your employer makes on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a corporate lawyer earning $108,352, the employer adds $13,002.24 in super each year. This is not deducted from your salary; it is paid into your super fund separately. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging can affect this.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates as a Floor

It is important to distinguish between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and market rates. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Award rates, such as those in the Legal Services Award, are higher than the national minimum. For a casual employee, the casual rate includes a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, a **corporate lawyer salary is almost always above these minimums. The [minimum wage](/blog) page provides the official figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Summary of Key Figures

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44/hr, $1,004.90/week (38 hrs)
- **Award Level 6 Law Clerk**: $36.03/hr (full-time)
- **ABS Average Full-Time Adult Ordinary Time**: $54.83/hr (approx.)
- **Casual Loading**: 25% on award rates only
- **Super**: 12% on ordinary earnings, paid on top

Use our [reference tables](/data) for a full list of rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
